translation: The heel bone (跟骨) is the bone of the heel of the foot; above it supports the ends of the hang (胻) and auxiliary (輔) bones, and a great sinew attaches to it, commonly called the foot-cramp sinew (腳攣筋). This sinew passes from the heel bone over the ankle bone, to the inside of the calf, up to the popliteal fossa (膕), passes the buttock, reaches the lumbar spine and the spine to the vertex, and from behind the head forward to the canthi of the eyes; all these are reached by this sinew. If one is injured by falling from a horse or from the stirrup, causing the heel bone to twist forward and the toes to turn backward, even if the bone is not broken but the seams separate, all the sinews from the foot to the lumbar spine lose their normal measure, cramping and painful; one should turn and rotate them back to their former state, and regulate and treat with medicines, all the same as the previous methods. [Note] The medicines Zhenggu Zijin Dan (Bone-Setting Purple-Gold Pill, 正骨紫金丹), Hunyuan Gao (Primordial Chaos Plaster, 混元膏), Sanyu Heshang Tang (Dispersing Stasis and Harmonizing Injury Decoction, 散瘀和傷湯), Haitongpi Tang (Erythrina Bark Decoction, 海桐皮湯), and Wanling Gao (Myriad-Efficacy Plaster, 萬靈膏) are all commonly used and proven formulas of the inner court, and therefore the above conditions mostly cite them.
